goal: Get PaddleSeg running on CPU: install PaddlePaddle (CPU) and the repo's dependencies, download data/optic_disc_seg (https://paddleseg.bj.bcebos.com/dataset/optic_disc_seg.zip, unzipped into PaddleSeg/data), then make `python tools/train.py --config configs/quick_start/pp_liteseg_optic_disc_512x512_1k.yml` train (a few iterations is enough, e.g. --iters 20 --batch_size 2) and `python tools/predict.py` on data/optic_disc_seg/JPEGImages/H0002.jpg with the saved model produce a segmentation image. /work/env.sh must activate the environment needed.
check: The hidden test trains briefly on CPU, runs prediction on an optic-disc image, and verifies that a model checkpoint and non-empty predicted mask images are written.

agent.final: DONE: on a clean rebuild, `setup.sh` gave a CPU PaddlePaddle 2.6.2 environment (Python 3.10, `numpy<2`), and a fresh shell sourcing `env.sh` trained 20 iterations (checkpoint at `output/iter_20/model.pdparams`) and predicted a non-empty two-class mask for H0002.jpg.
